jobs.title: Measure Nano (XNO) confirmation time and publish the method
jobs.description: Send at least 50 small XNO transactions from an account you control and record, for each one, the wall-clock interval between broadcast and the point at which a public node reports the block confirmed. Publish a public repository or gist containing the raw per-transaction measurements (one row per send: timestamp, block hash, node queried, milliseconds to confirmation), the script that produced them, and a short README stating which node(s) you used. We are not asking you to argue that Nano is fast; we are asking for numbers a reader can reproduce with your script.
acceptance: A public URL contains a script that a reader can run without editing it, other than supplying their own account.
The published data has at least 50 rows, each with a block hash, a node host, and an integer millisecond measurement.
Every published block hash resolves on a public Nano explorer.
The README names the node(s) queried and the date range of the measurements.
The median and 95th percentile are stated and are derivable from the published rows.

jobs.title: Adversarially review dhyabi2/nano-settlement-verify against its own README
jobs.description: Read https://github.com/dhyabi2/nano-settlement-verify and try to break it. We want the cases its test suite does not cover: inputs where it reports a settlement that did not happen, or refuses one that did. Deliver a public write-up listing each finding with the exact input that triggers it and the observed versus expected behaviour. A finding must be reproducible from your write-up alone. Reporting that you found nothing is an acceptable delivery if you show what you tried.
acceptance: A public URL contains a write-up naming the commit SHA of the code reviewed.
Each finding states an exact input, the observed behaviour, and the expected behaviour.
Each finding is reproducible by following only the write-up, with no further questions.
A finding of 'no defects found' is accompanied by the list of cases attempted.
The write-up does not require access to any system we own.

jobs.title: Port the Nano address checksum validator to TypeScript, with the same known-answer vectors
jobs.description: Port vendor/nanoaddr.py from this repository to TypeScript with no runtime dependencies. Same public surface: validate(address) returns a verdict object with the same reason codes (bad_prefix, bad_length, bad_padding, bad_character, bad_checksum), and encode(publicKey) returns the same address. Deliver a public repository with the source and a test file.
acceptance: A public URL contains TypeScript source with no runtime dependencies in package.json.
validate() returns the same reason code as the Python original for each of: wrong prefix, wrong length, bad first character, a character outside the Nano base32 alphabet, and an altered checksum.
The all-zero public key encodes to the canonical burn address nano_1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111hifc8npp.
Changing any single character of a valid address makes validate() return valid: false.
The test file runs green from a clean clone with one documented command.
